summary.short: Sets detailed procedural rules for Commission proceedings under the Digital Markets Act: form and content of gatekeeper notifications and submissions, document format and length, right to be heard, access to file, confidentiality and time limits. Enters into force on 2 May 2023.
summary.long: Adopted 14 April 2023 under Article 46(1) of the Digital Markets Act (Regulation (EU) 2022/1925), this Regulation sets detailed procedural rules for Commission proceedings under that Regulation. Chapter II governs notifications and submissions by undertakings providing core platform services, including gatekeeper notifications on the Annex I form, substantiated arguments under Article 3(5) and the duty to provide correct, complete and non-misleading information; incomplete submissions take effect only once complete. Annex II sets format and page limits, such as 50 pages per distinct core platform service for a gatekeeper notification. Chapter III allows the Commission to open proceedings up to its preliminary findings and makes the opening public. Chapter IV covers the right to be heard: time-limited written observations, business-secret protection and access to the file, including unredacted access for specified external counsel and experts under Commission-set disclosure terms. Chapter V sets time periods that begin on the working day following the triggering event (Article 9(2)) and allows extensions on reasoned request. Digital transmission is the default. The Regulation is binding in all Member States and enters into force on 2 May 2023.

thresholds.note: The text refers to the Article 3(2) DMA thresholds (turnover, market capitalisation, monthly active end users, yearly active business users) but states no values. Its numeric limits are procedural: page limits in Annex II (50, 30, 30 and 50 pages), a 4 700 characters-per-page format limit, one-week periods (Arts 7(6) and 8(5)) and a three-year period in Art 8(3)(c). These were not coded as thresholds because they are document format or time limits, not cutoffs that change legal treatment.
